$comment: The single source of truth for release-eligibility behaviour. Both the data-driven TUnit suite
(EligibilityScenarioTests) and the `just release-matrix` recipe, which runs each case through
the real CLI, read this file. Adding a rule or a policy means appending cases here, not
Fields: version (as written in package.json), ref (the evaluated git ref), policy, strictness,
existingTags, publishedVersions (null means the feed was not consulted), and the expected
verdict / ruleId / exitCode. ruleId is the rule that decided the verdict, or null when every

scenarios.name: model-a-untagged-stable-releases
scenarios.why: Today's Model A: every consuming repository releases a stable version from main.

scenarios.name: model-a-already-tagged-skips
scenarios.why: Replaces the workflow's `git rev-parse` gate. Already released is a skip, not a failure.

scenarios.name: model-a-prerelease-from-main-releases
scenarios.why: sourcegenerator-framework, value-objects and zodsharp ship prereleases from main.

scenarios.name: model-a-patch-from-main-releases
scenarios.why: REL004 is not enabled in ReleaseOnMain, so patches keep shipping from main.

scenarios.name: model-b-stable-from-release-branch-releases
scenarios.why: The documented main-as-head model releases from the `release` branch.

scenarios.name: model-a-stable-from-feature-branch-fails
scenarios.why: REL003: a stable version may only come from a declared release head.

scenarios.name: model-c-stable-from-release-line-releases
scenarios.why: Model C: a serviced stable line releases 2.0.2 from release/2.0.

scenarios.name: model-c-prerelease-from-next-line-releases
scenarios.why: Model C: an in-flight prerelease line releases 2.1.0-prerelease.1 from release/2.1, with the 2.0 line untouched.

scenarios.name: model-c-stable-from-main-fails
scenarios.why: Model C reserves trunk: merging to main must not ship anything.

scenarios.name: model-c-patch-from-main-fails-rel004
scenarios.why: REL004: a non-zero PATCH is serviced from the line's release branch, never trunk. Reached only because the version is a prerelease, so REL003 does not short-circuit first.

scenarios.name: model-c-version-regression-fails-rel005
scenarios.why: REL005: the version must advance past the highest existing version on its own line.

scenarios.name: model-c-other-line-does-not-block-rel005
scenarios.why: REL005 is scoped to the line, so a higher 2.1 version does not block a 2.0 patch.

scenarios.name: four-part-passes-under-nuget-strictness
scenarios.why: aspirec4 (13.5.3.10) and build-sdk (1.0.2.2) ship four-part versions today.

scenarios.name: four-part-fails-under-semver2-strictness
scenarios.why: REL001: SemVer2 strictness is the opt-in stricter setting that rejects four-part versions.

scenarios.name: four-part-fails-rel006-without-allowfourpart
scenarios.why: REL006 enabled by a policy that does not permit four-part versions.

scenarios.name: four-part-passes-rel006-from-four-part-ref
scenarios.why: FourPartServicing permits four-part versions from a release branch.

scenarios.name: four-part-fails-rel006-from-wrong-ref
scenarios.why: REL006 also constrains WHERE a four-part version may be released from.

scenarios.name: unparseable-version-fails-rel001
scenarios.why: The old VersionModule threw and the tool exited 1.

scenarios.name: already-published-version-skips
scenarios.why: REL002's feed half, when a simulated published-version list is supplied.

scenarios.name: tag-skip-and-policy-fail-have-distinct-exit-codes
scenarios.why: A policy violation must not be mistakable for an already-released skip.

expected.whyThisOrder: REL002 precedes REL003, so an already-released version skips before the ref is judged.

$policiesComment: Extra policies the scenarios above select, beyond the built-in ReleaseOnMain,
TrunkReservesMinor and FourPartServicing. Written into the generated purview-build.json
for the CLI matrix, and bound directly by the TUnit suite.
